name: Clover-Sanctum

civilization.name: The Verdant Concord
civilization.notes: A pacifist agrarian civilization of garden-city builders who terraformed their own biosphere into a paradise and export ecological restoration expertise to other worlds.

description: Clover-Sanctum is what engineers produce when they refuse to choose between technology and wilderness: tiered garden cities of living wood and glass rise no higher than the surrounding canopy, and rivers run deliberately wild through the centers of towns. The Coriander Range guards the southern hemisphere with snow-crowned peaks, while the northern rift valleys hold terraced lakes connected by cascades that power the civilization's graceful energy grid. From orbit the continents look less inhabited than embroidered.

Days follow a liturgy of light—dawn bells sounded from vine-wrapped towers, afternoon rains that arrive punctually enough to set chronometers by, and evenings when millions of cultivated glowmoths are released to pollinate the night gardens. The air carries bread, blossoms, and clean ozone from the storm-breakers along the coasts. Even the cities are quiet, because the Verdant Concord considers noise a form of waste.

The Concord's histories begin eight thousand years ago with 'the Inheritance': a functioning paradise their oldest texts claim they did not build. Scattered across the least accessible plateaus stand monoliths of impossible black material that predate every Concord record, and twice a decade, deep receivers buried beside the subterranean ocean capture a repeating signal that translates as a single word in no known language. The Concord tends these sites like graves and forbids all excavation.

Outsiders prize Clover-Sanctum for its ecological sciences, and its Restoration Corps is welcomed on dying worlds across the sector—but diplomatic access stops at the plateau fences, and the Concord does not explain why. Smugglers whisper that the monoliths are doors, that the signal is counting, and that the Concord's serene refusal to leave their homeworld is not philosophy but obedience. Whatever the truth, the Concord has begun, for the first time in recorded history, to buy starships.
